posts.title: 2027 PC Game Requirements: Every Published Spec
posts.excerpt: 19 upcoming PC games have published system requirements. Their GPU, RAM, storage and Windows needs, side by side and sourced from Steam.
posts.content:
19 games due in 2027 or announced for PC have already published system requirements, out of the 50 upcoming titles we track. Together they set a clear bar: 16GB is the most common minimum amount of memory, the middle minimum graphics card is roughly Intel Arc A580 class, and 10 of the 14 recommended specs that state memory ask for 16GB.

Below is every published spec side by side, followed by the details that are easy to miss — the games that need Windows 11, the ones that insist on an SSD, and how much space they take.

Graphics cards: minimum and recommended

Most demanding first, ranked by the minimum card each publisher names. The wording is the publisher's.

The spread is wide. SAW: Genesis names NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 as its minimum — the highest floor of any game here — while Pony Island 2: Panda Circus starts at NVIDIA GeForce GTX 550 Ti. At the top of the recommended column, Lords of the Fallen II asks for AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT.

2 games with published requirements do not name a graphics card at all yet, and 5 name no recommended card.

Memory

8 ask for 16GB, 3 ask for 12GB, 5 ask for 8GB, 1 asks for 6GB and 2 ask for 4GB as a minimum. For the recommended tier, 16GB is close to universal; Chrono Odyssey and Sea of Remnants recommend 32GB. The full breakdown is in how much RAM and storage 2027 games need.

Storage and SSDs

15 games state an install size, from 3GB to 135GB, with a median of 30GB. Fable, SAW: Genesis and The Talos Principle 3 mention an SSD in their requirements.

Windows 11 only

SAW: Genesis, Star Trek: Shadow Frontier and Lords of the Fallen II list Windows 11 and no earlier version. Every other game here that names an operating system still accepts Windows 10.

Check your own PC

Every game above has its own page with the full publisher table, and the checker compares your graphics card, processor and memory against it directly. Start from the full list of 2027 releases, or see which graphics cards clear these specs.

Where these numbers come from

Every requirement quoted here is the publisher's own, read from the game's Steam store page on 12 September 2026. Placeholder entries — "TBD", "TBA", "Coming soon" — are treated as not published, never as a spec. Where we compare a graphics card or processor against a requirement, we use the performance index described in our editorial standards. We re-read every listing monthly, and this article is regenerated from that data each time, so its figures move when the publishers' do.

posts.title: Best GPU for 2027 Games, by Published Requirements
posts.excerpt: Which graphics cards clear the minimum and recommended specs of upcoming 2027 PC games — compared against 14 published requirements, not guesses.
posts.content:
The cheapest graphics card that clears every recommended spec published for a 2027 PC game so far is the AMD Radeon RX 9070, which launched at $549. On a tighter budget, the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 ($299 at launch) meets the recommended card for 9 of 14 games and the minimum for 16 of 17.

That answer comes from comparing each card against the requirements publishers have actually posted, not from predictions. 17 of the 50 upcoming games we track name a minimum graphics card and 14 name a recommended one.

How popular cards compare

"Minimum met" counts the games whose minimum card your card matches or beats in our performance index; "recommended met" does the same for the recommended card. Where a publisher states a VRAM amount, the card must have at least that much.

The picks

  • Clears every recommended spec: AMD Radeon RX 9070 — the lowest launch price of any card that matches or beats all 14 recommended cards.
  • Best value under $350: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 — the most recommended specs met (9) at that price.
  • Clears every minimum: AMD Radeon RX 7700 XT ($449 at launch). One game sets that bar on its own: SAW: Genesis names NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 as its minimum. Leave it out, and the Intel Arc B580 ($249) meets every other minimum.

What "meets the recommended spec" does not tell you

Publishers rarely say what resolution, settings or frame rate a recommended card is meant to deliver, so clearing it is a sign a card is in the right class — not a promise of 60 frames per second at 1440p. For a frame-rate estimate on a specific game, use the FPS estimator; to see where any card ranks overall, see the GPU tier list 2027.

Memory matters too: 12 of the 14 games that state a recommended amount ask for 16GB or more. Details are in how much RAM and storage 2027 games need.

Where these numbers come from

Every requirement quoted here is the publisher's own, read from the game's Steam store page on 12 September 2026. Placeholder entries — "TBD", "TBA", "Coming soon" — are treated as not published, never as a spec. Where we compare a graphics card or processor against a requirement, we use the performance index described in our editorial standards. We re-read every listing monthly, and this article is regenerated from that data each time, so its figures move when the publishers' do.

Launch MSRP is the manufacturer's price at release, in US dollars — not today's price, which we do not track.

posts.title: How Much RAM and Storage Do 2027 PC Games Need?
posts.excerpt: 16GB of RAM meets every published 2027 minimum, but not every recommended spec. Memory, install sizes and SSD needs for upcoming PC games, from Steam.
posts.content:
16GB of RAM covers every 2027 PC game that has published its requirements so far — at the minimum. 8 of the 19 games that state a minimum ask for exactly 16GB, the most common figure, and none asks for more than 16GB. The recommended tier is where 16GB stops being enough for everyone: Chrono Odyssey and Sea of Remnants recommend 32GB.

Storage varies far more than memory — from 3GB to 135GB — and a handful of games now name an SSD outright.

posts.title: Most Wishlisted Upcoming PC Games and Their Specs
posts.excerpt: The most wishlisted upcoming PC games on Steam, with each one's release window and whether it has published system requirements yet — sourced, not guessed.
posts.content:
4 of the 8 most wishlisted upcoming PC games we track have published their system requirements — Fable, SAW: Genesis, Guild Wars 3 and Lords of the Fallen II. That is a higher share than upcoming games overall, where 19 of 50 have posted specs: the biggest launches tend to publish sooner.

The rankings are not ours. We list a game here only when a named source ranked it, and link that source, so nothing on this page is our guess at what is popular.

Why 4 of them have no specs yet

A Steam page can go live years before launch, and publishers usually post requirements late, once the game is close to final. Until then the store page often carries placeholders — "TBD", "Coming soon" — which we do not treat as requirements. Each game's page here says plainly that nothing has been published, and fills in the day the listing changes.

What the ones with published specs ask for

  • Fable: minimum AMD Radeon RX 6600 / Nvidia RTX 5050 / NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 / Intel A580, 12GB RAM, 135GB storage.
  • SAW: Genesis: minimum NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 8GB, 16GB RAM, 15GB storage, Windows 11 only.
  • Guild Wars 3: minimum RTX 2060 / Radeon RX 5700 / Intel Arc A580, 16GB RAM, 65GB storage.
  • Lords of the Fallen II: minimum NVIDIA RTX-2060 / AMD Radeon RX 5700, 12GB RAM, Windows 11 only.

Rankings used

  • In GameDiscoverCo's top 10 most-wishlisted Steam games from Summer Game Fest 2026
  • Jumped to No. 3 in Steam wishlist adds after its June 2026 date reveal (~125k)
